title: "Missing Submit Button" error displayed while a form is loading
body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary While a form is loading, for a brief moment "Missing Submit Button" error flashes on the screen. ### Reproducible Code Example From official examples: https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/execution-flow/st.form ```Python import streamlit as st with st.form("my_form"): st.write("Inside the form") slider_val = st.slider("Form slider") checkbox_val = st.checkbox("Form checkbox") # Every form must have a submit button. submitted = st.form_submit_button("Submit") if submitted: st.write("slider", slider_val, "checkbox", checkbox_val) st.write("Outside the form") ``` ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Navigate to the official form example: https://doc-form1.streamlit.app/ 2. Turn on browser developer tools (I am using Chrome in this example) 3. Select "Disable cache" 4. Select "Slow 4G" throttling 5. Refresh the page 6. Observe a big red error message "Missing Submit Button" After the form finishes loading it works fine. ### Expected Behavior While a form is loading, no error messages should be displayed. ### Current Behavior While a form is loading, for a brief moment "Missing Submit Button" error flashes on the screen. ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.55.0 - Python version: 3.12.12 - Operating System: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS - Browser: Chrome, Firefox ### Additional Information _No response_

**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-14247)

This is a valid bug in the `st.form` frontend component. During initial page load on slow connections, the "Missing Submit Button" error briefly flashes because the form renders before all its child elements (including the submit button) have been received from the backend.

**Root cause:** The `Form` component in `frontend/lib/src/components/widgets/Form/Form.tsx` checks whether to show the "Missing Submit Button" warning based on two conditions: (1) no submit button is registered in `formsData`, and (2) `scriptRunState === ScriptRunState.NOT_RUNNING`. The problem is that `NOT_RUNNING` is the **default initial state** (see `ScriptRunContext.tsx` line 70 and the commented-out `INITIAL` state in `ScriptRunState.ts` lines 18-21). On slow connections, there's a window where the form component renders with `NOT_RUNNING` before the script has actually started running — the frontend cannot distinguish "script hasn't started yet" from "script has finished." This causes the form to incorrectly conclude the script completed without a submit button, flashing the error until the script actually runs and delivers the submit button delta.

### Related Issues

- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13002 — Request to disable sidebar rendering until page load is complete. Same class of problem: premature rendering of UI elements/errors before the backend script has finished executing.
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5798 — Request to optimize static file loading and reduce app startup time. Faster loading would reduce the window during which this flash occurs, though it wouldn't fix the root cause.
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11010 — Reports flickering and weird behavior during page load in multipage apps after upgrade. Related to the general theme of visual glitches during the loading phase.

Hi, I’d like to work on this issue.

From what I observed, the warning is triggered before child components (including the submit button) are fully mounted, which leads to a transient false positive during initial render.

I’ve implemented a fix by moving the validation logic into a useEffect and delaying it until after the initial mount.

This approach eliminates the flicker while preserving the existing behavior when a submit button is actually missing.

Happy to open a PR if this aligns with the intended behavior.
